environment: GCC 14.2 Release -O3; shared AMD EPYC 9V74 VM, four-CPU quota; llvmpipe software Vulkan; no physical GPU
scope: Native synthetic general-3D benchmarks; 60 warmup +90 measured frames, 320x180, VSync off. Diagnostic wrappers use existing render-control and shadow-settings APIs; engine implementation objects are unchanged.

findings.topic: Opaque pipeline selection and lighting parity
findings.evidence: Default ForwardPlus submits visible opaque meshes to both G-buffer and forward shading. Hybrid omits the second mesh shading submission for supported core opaque materials; observed requests fall from about 2008 to 1004 per frame, excluding fullscreen passes.
findings.confound: Lighting modes are not visually equivalent: Forward+ hemisphere GI and wrap fill in mesh3d.frag differ from flat ambient in deferred_lighting.frag; other shading/AA differences were not isolated. The measured gain cannot be attributed solely to removing duplicate geometry, nor claimed as a behavior-preserving optimization.
findings.next: Define shared core-lighting behavior and image tolerance, then A/B ForwardPlus and Hybrid on hardware GPU with per-pass timing and mesh/triangle/skin counters. Preserve forward fallback for unsupported material features.

findings.evidence: Frame graph builds seven shadow clear attachments plus G-buffer even when no shadow caster submits geometry. Prior profiler has exactly eight pass recordings per parallel frame. Default logical extent is seven 2048x2048 D32 layers.
findings.experiment: Changing only unused atlas size to 512 through existing settings preserves captures and state hashes. Timing results include reversals and a large outlier; no stable general-frame gain established.
findings.next: Measure empty-pass cost directly before redesigning active-layer scheduling. Any change must preserve initialization, image layouts, in-flight slot fences, cached local layers and shadow-on/off transitions.
findings.caveat: Logical attachment extent is not measured memory traffic; hardware can implement fast clears.

findings.evidence: Two unprofiled runs per mode show roughly 102-104 ms means with no stable benefit. Serial diagnostic record scope is 1.426 ms; earlier auto scope was about 1.656 ms in a different run.
findings.next: Do not prioritize changing the scheduler based on current evidence. Existing adaptive policy compares serial cost with 500 microseconds, not measured parallel speedup; periodic sampling improvements remain a candidate requiring CPU-bound hardware evidence.

limitations: All time measurements are software-Vulkan results; they do not predict hardware-GPU performance.
RenderTrace counts high-level mesh submission requests, not independently measured vkCmdDraw invocations or vertex shader executions. Fullscreen lighting/postprocess draws are excluded.
First diagnostic runs include three untimed capture frames in trace totals; timed phase metrics still cover only 90 measured frames. Counter summaries use runs without captures.
Shadow atlas resizing is a diagnostic control, not a proposed quality reduction for enabled shadows.
No production implementation or rendering defaults were changed.
